question: According to the Charter Act of 1853, how many legislative members were there in the Council of the Governor General?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Charter Act of 1853 marked the last legislative measure under the East India Company before the governance of India was transferred to the British Crown.
 
• Under the Charter Act of 1853, the Council of the Governor-General was expanded to include **6 new legislative members**.
 
• It introduced a separate legislative council known as the Legislative Council of India, which had **4 members** for legislative purposes.
 
• The Act is significant for separating the executive and legislative functions of the Governor-General's Council.
 
• This was the first instance of introducing a systematic legislative process in British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Charter Act of 1853:**

 
 
• It was the last Charter Act passed by the British Parliament related to the governance of India.
 
• It extended the tenure of the East India Company without specifying an end date, unlike previous Charter Acts.
 
• It allowed Indians to compete in the civil services examination for the first time.
 
• It introduced an open competition system for recruiting civil servants, laying the foundation for modern bureaucracy.
 
 
 
• **Governor-General's Legislative Council:**
 
 
• It was created to assist the Governor-General in formulating legislative policies.
 
• The legislative members were nominated and included British officials and representatives.
 
• Its establishment paved the way for more structured legislative processes in India.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Charter Act of 1853:**
 
 
• It significantly contributed to the modernization of Indian administration.
 
• The Act set the foundation for the establishment of a more systematic legal and legislative framework.
 
• The separation of powers between legislative and executive functions became a key administrative reform.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Act was passed during the declining years of the East India Company’s rule in India.
 
• It was one of the critical legislative measures leading up to the Government of India Act of 1858.
 
• The reforms under this Act reflected the British Parliament's increased control over Indian governance.
